items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1995-08-29
items.q: You got Big Joe Turner coming in.

ctx.x: Okay, real number four with Tex Stevens, and this is still August 29th, 1995. Okay, uh, yeah, uh, where were we? Were we talking about Frank Panae? We were moving along. Well in 19...

...his... Right after the soldiers started coming home, and then some soldiers were passing through, and like we said, things were not as integrated as they are now, and people wanted to... People had a few money. Some people were covered being, uh, turned loose and normal with three, four, five, six hundred dollars, which was a lot of money. Remember, Coca-Cola was 25 cents, uh, Coca-Cola was five cents a bottle. You could get a half a pint of liquor for 45 cents, along with a seven-up of Coke and a pitcher of…
He had the whole package. He had the package.

items.title: George "Tex" Stephens Interview, 1996-08-23
items.q: But he stayed at the Dewdrop Hotel because that's where he was playing with Frank Pannier.

ctx.x: Because this was what you would call spiritual rejuvenation. A lot of people didn't understand what was happening with the blues, especially some of the white bands who just started picking up on the blues into the late 80s, that the blues really came out of the black church. And, well, prior to that, the sacrifices that blacks made were harmed from the soul because they paid so many dues. And then, as I talked with my old great uncles from way back when they spoke with their ancestors and relatives during the…
Did that cause the demise of that club? Because I don't think it...
